That in the Psalms it is said: From the depths I cried to you, Lord. He sat down, I have already said it, because he humiliated himself. 10. And a woman arrives. It is a figure of the Church, no longer justified, but which will soon be justified, since the conversation will deal with this matter. And she comes without knowing anything and finds Jesus, and Jesus starts a conversation with her. Let's see what conversation and why. A woman from Samaria arrives to draw water. The Samaritans did not belong to the Jewish nation; They were aliens, although they lived in surrounding regions. As it would take a long time to relate their origin and I would dwell on many things, without saying them all, it is enough for us to consider the Samaritans as foreigners. And lest it be thought that I affirm this with more boldness than truth, listen to what the Lord Jesus says about that Samaritan, one of the ten lepers whom the Lord cleansed from leprosy and the only one who returned to thank him: Were there not ten cleansed from leprosy? So where are the other nine? No one returned to thank him, except for this foreigner. The coming of this foreign woman, who was a figure of the Church, is a symbol of reality, because it would be formed from the Gentiles, people strange to the Jews. The Samaritan women, in fact, used these books and lived according to the same Law, and hence they also had circumcision. But since it is very difficult for me to explain what follows: And now the husband you have is not yours, it seems easier to me to see in these five first husbands of the soul the five senses of the body. Well, when one is born, before he can use reason and mind, he is not governed except by the senses of the body. The soul of a child only desires or rejects what it hears, or sees, or smells, or tastes, or feels. Only desire what pleases, and refuse everything that displeases these five senses. Because these five senses like pleasure and dislike pain. The soul begins to live subject to the law of these five senses, which are like five husbands; they govern it. Why are they called husbands? Because they are legitimate; They are God's workmanship and a gift that God makes to the soul. The soul that is governed by these five senses and that acts according to the law of these five husbands is still weak. But when the dawn of reason comes to him, if he then receives an excellent education and the science of wisdom, he will see how he takes the lead, instead of those five husbands, he! only true and legitimate command, and better than them, and that governs it better: governs it for eternity, and cultivates it for eternity, and instructs it for eternity. These five senses do not govern us for eternity; They only govern us in the desire or hatred of temporal goods. But from the moment the understanding, moved by wisdom, takes the reins in the direction of the soul, it realizes that life is no longer just fleeing from precipices and walking on flat land, which is what the eyes of the still weak soul reveal; that life is not reduced solely to hearing harmonious voices with pleasure and discordant voices with pleasure, or to delight in pleasant odors or to be disgusted with unpleasant ones, or to feel attractive for what is sweet or repugnant for what is bitter, or to experience the caresses of the soft or the harshness of the rough. All of these are necessary experiences of the soul that is still sick. What function, then, is that of reason? He will discern not the white from the black, but the just from the unjust, the good from the bad, the useful from the useless, chastity from impudence (one to love it and the other to avoid it), the; hate: one so that it remains and the other so that it disappears. 22.

He now eagerly desires to drink his fill of that water; To announce Christ, he leaves his load there and runs to the city to say to those men: Come and see the man who has told me everything I have done. What a precaution to avoid the fury, indignation and persecution of those people: Come and see the man who has told me everything I have done! Could this not be the Christ? The people leave the city and go to Him.,!; |; 31. Meanwhile, the disciples pestered him, saying: Rabbi, eat. They had gone shopping and were already back. But He said to them: I have a delicacy to eat of which you do not know. The disciples said to each other: Has someone brought him something to eat? What surprise, then, that the woman did not understand water, when not even the disciples themselves understood the delicacy? The Lord sees his thoughts and lacks time to teach them as a teacher, not by detour, as he did with that woman, who urgently demanded the presence of her husband, but clearly: My food, he says, is to do the will of the one who sent me. Then his drink was also to fulfill with that woman the will of the one who sent him.

That is the meaning of those words: I am thirsty; give me a drink, to produce faith in you and drink your faith and incorporate you into my body; my body is the Church: This, then, he says, is my food: to do the will of him who sent me.

32. Don't you say: There are still four months left and the harvest is coming? He was burning with desire to carry out his work and urgently needed to send workers. You count four months until the harvest; Well, I show you another harvest, all white and in season. Here is what I tell you: Raise your eyes and look at the white fields, all already ready for harvest. Then you have to send reapers. In these circumstances the adage is verified: One is the one who sows and another is the one who reaps; and one enjoys the same as the other. I send you to reap what you did not till; Others worked it and you got involved in their work, you. What then? Did He send reapers and not sowers? Where did he send the reapers? There where others had already worked. Well, where there had been work there had also been sowing. And the seed cast on the ground was already ripe and was already asking for the sickle and the threshing. Where should the reapers be sent? Where the prophets had already preached; they were the sowers. Well, if they were not the sowers, where did the news come to that woman: I know that the Messiah is about to arrive? That woman was already ripe fruit, the crops were already all white and they asked for the sickle. I; Well, I have sent you. Where to? To reap what you did not sow. Those who planted were others and you got involved in their work. What were the patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob? Read their works. All these works are a prophecy of Christ; That's why they were sowers. Moses, and the other patriarchs, and all the prophets, how much they had to suffer in the cold of the fields! Then in Judea the harvest was already in season. In truth, that harvest was already in season, when so many thousands of men carried the price of their goods and deposited it at the feet of the apostles, and, their shoulders lightened by secular burdens, they went in pursuit of the Lord Jesus Christ. Truly it was already harvest in full maturity. What was done next? They threw grains of that harvest into the earth, and the world was sown and another harvest sprouted, which will be reaped at the end of the centuries. It is of this harvest that it is said: Those who sow with tears will reap full of joy. The reapers of this harvest will not be the apostles, but the angels. The reapers, he says, are the angels. This harvest grows with the tares and eagerly awaits their separation at the end of the world. That other harvest was already in full maturity; that, I say, where the disciples were first sent and the prophets worked.

Consider, however, brothers, what is said: That he who sows and he who reaps enjoys the same thing. The work was done at different times, but they enjoyed the same happiness together; They received the same reward together: eternal life.

I only have to notice once that the reading is finished. The woman was the one who first broke the news; Then the Samaritans believed because of the woman's testimony, and finally, the Samaritans urged her to stay with them, and she stayed with them for two days and many more believed. And after they had believed, they said to the woman We no longer believe because of your word, but we have seen him and know in truth that this is the Savior of the world. First for fame and then for presence. The same thing happens today to those who are outside and are not Christians: Christian friends begin to give them news of Christ, as that woman, symbol of the Church, did; then they come to Christ, that is, they believe in Christ because of this news, and, finally, he stays with them for two days, that is, he gives them the two precepts of charity; and with this many more believe, and more firmly, that He is truly the Savior of the world.

From those words: "Two days later he left there for Galilee", to those others: "And he and all his family believed" 1. The reading of this Gospel passage that I propose to explain today is a continuation of the passage that was read yesterday. The meaning of such a passage is not difficult to penetrate, but it is very worthy of explanation, admiration and praise. So I will only make a recommendatory commemoration of this Gospel passage, not a difficult exposition. Jesus, after two days in Samaria, went to Galilee, where he had grown up. The evangelist adds: Jesus himself testifies that no prophet is honored in his homeland. Jesus left Samaria after two days, not because he did not receive honors there. Jesus' homeland was not Samaria, but Galilee. How is it that, having left there so soon to move to Galilee, where he had grown up, he testifies

It seems that he would have been able to testify with more reason that no prophet is honored in his country if, disdaining to go to Galilee, he had remained in Samaria. 2. Let your charity now be attentive to the no small difficulty that is suggested here. The Lord will inspire me and grant me what I have to say. You know the difficulty; now look for its solution; I will repeat the difficulty so that the solution becomes more desirable. It surprises me why the evangelist says: Well, Jesus himself testifies that no prophet is honored in his country. Puzzled by this, we repeat the preceding words to find out why the evangelist meant this. And I find that in the previous words it says nothing other than that Jesus, after two days, leaves Samaria to go to Galilee. The reason why you said, O evangelist, that Jesus testifies that no prophet is honored in his country, was because, after two days, he leaves Samaria and hurries to go to Galilee? To me, on the contrary, it seems more logical to say that, if Jesus was not honored in his homeland, there was no reason to return to it so quickly and leave Samaria. But, if I am not deceived, I will better say, it is true and I am not deceived, because the evangelist knew better than I what he was saying, and the one who drank it from the Lord's own breast saw the truth better than I. In fact, John the Evangelist is the same one who, among all the disciples, rested on the Lord's breast, and for whom the Lord, who loved everyone, had, however, a special predilection. Then would he be the one deceived and would it be me who tells the truth? Everything the opposite; and if I want to think religiously, I have to listen with docility to what he says, to merit the intelligence of what he thinks. 3. Hear, then, dear ones, what I think on this point, without any prevention against what you think, if it is more accurate. the truth. He was in Samaria for two days and the Samaritans believed in Him; however, with so many in Galilee, the Galileans did not believe in Him. Go back in your memory and remember the reading and the explanation of yesterday, where the woman with whom he discussed such great mysteries had begun to announce him.

So the Samaritans saw and heard him, believed in him through the word of the woman, and even more firmly and in greater numbers believed in him because of his word: thus it is written. He stayed there for two days (this number is mystically a recommendation of the two precepts that contain the entire law and the prophets).

Well, when there in Cana of Galilee He turned water into wine, only His disciples believed in Him, as John says, and the house was certainly full of invited people. Although the prodigy he performed was so great, no one believed in him, except for his disciples. Jesus now returns to this city of Galilee for the second time. And behold, a courtier, who had a sick son of his, came to Jesus and began to implore him to come down to that city or to his house to heal his son, who was dying. Whoever asked like this, didn't he still believe? What do you want me to tell you? Ask the Lord what he judges of him. The Lord, to the request of the ruler, answers in this way: If you do not see signs and wonders, you do not believe. He reproaches this man for his lukewarmness or coldness or for his total lack of faith; but eager to prove by the healing of his son what Christ was like and who Christ was and how much his power. We have heard the word of the one who prays; but we do not see the heart of the one who distrusts; but he who heard his word and saw his heart testifies to it. Finally, the same evangelist also shows, with the testimony of his narration, that he still did not believe who wanted the Lord to come to his house to heal his son. Because after he received the announcement of his son's healing and that this had happened at the same hour that the Lord said: Come, your son is alive, he believed, says the evangelist, he and his entire family. Then, if he and his entire family believed because of the announcement of his son's health and because of the comparison he made between the time of those who announced it to him and the time of the one who announced it to him in advance, when he suppliantly urged him, they did not believe. The Samaritans, on the other hand, do not expect any miracles; They only believe his word. This is why his compatriots became worthy of this reproach: If you do not see signs and wonders, you do not believe; and right there, after such a great miracle, only he and his family believed. Because of the words alone, many Samaritans believed, and, on the other hand, with such a great miracle only the family where it was performed believed. What is it, then, brothers, what is the lesson that the Lord wants to give you? Galilee, which is part of Judea, was Jesus' homeland at that time, because he grew up there. But now it is seen that those events were predictions of something.

Miracles are not called prodigies except because they predict or foreshadow something. The word prodigy has the same meaning as porrodicio (something said in advance), which is like a prediction, announcement or significance of something future. Look now at the Jewish mob, look at those people already scattered throughout the world and uprooted to their roots, and look at their broken, cut, scattered, and dried branches, in whose cuts the wild olive deserved to be grafted; Look, I say, at the Jewish people, and what do they say now? Well, although one of the twelve chosen and holy ones was, without a doubt, an Israelite, that is, one of the Lord's people, that Thomas who wanted to insert his fingers into the openings of the wounds. The Lord rebukes him the same as the courtier. Say to this one: If you do not see signs and wonders, you do not believe. Say to him: Because you have seen, you have believed. Jesus had returned to Galilee after having left the Samaritans, who believed because of his words without performing any miracles in his presence; and he leaves them so soon, sure of his firmness in faith, because he did not cease to be in them with the presence of divinity. When, then, the Lord said to Thomas: Come near and introduce your hand and be no longer unbelieving, but faithful; and when he, after touching the place of the wounds, exclaims saying: My Lord and my God!, he rebukes him with. these words: Because you have seen, you have believed; Why this, if not because the prophet has no honor in his country?

On the other hand, because this prophet is honored among foreigners, it is said next: Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed. The prediction looks to us. What the Lord praised with so much anticipation, He has deigned to accomplish in us. Those who crucified him saw and felt him,

6. How then does the number forty mean perfect work? Perhaps because the law is the ten precepts; law that would be preached throughout the world. The world is divided into four parts: east, west, south and north; the number ten, multiplied by four, adds up to forty; or because the Gospel, which consists of four books, completes the law. In the Gospel it is said: I have not come to destroy the law, but to complete it. Whether that is the cause or another more probable one that is hidden from us, but not from the most learned, the truth, however, is that the number forty means a certain perfection in good works, which consists, above all, in the exercise of abstinence from the illicit lusts of the century, that is, in general fasting. Listen also to the Apostle, who says: The fullness of the law is charity. What is its principle? The grace of God, the Holy Spirit. We do not have it of ourselves as being its authors; It is a gift from God, and great; since the charity of God, he says, has been diffused into our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. Charity is perfect fulfillment of the law; That is why it is most truthfully said: The fullness of the law is charity. Let us go in search of charity, as the Lord recommends it to us. Remember my purpose: I want to explain the number thirty-eight, which was the age of that sick person: why the number thirty-eighth indicates illness rather than health. Therefore, as I just said, charity is the perfect fulfillment of the law. The number forty indicates the complete fulfillment of the law in all works; and charity is recommended to us in two precepts. Consider carefully, I beg you, and engrave in your memory what I am saying: do not despise the words, lest your soul be like a road where the thrown seed does not germinate and the birds of the sky come, he says, and take it away. Understand this well and hide it in the most intimate part of your hearts. There are two precepts of charity recommended by the Lord: You will love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul and with all your mind, and you will love your neighbor as yourself. These two commandments are the entire Law and the Prophets. With what good sense that poor widow put into the gifts of God two small coins, which were all her assets!

It has the same meaning that the innkeeper received two silver coins to care for that sick man wounded by the thieves, and the same thing also means that Jesus stayed with the Samaritans for two days to strengthen them in charity. Whenever, therefore, the number two means a good work, it is, above all, a recommendation of the precept of charity.

If, then, the number forty means the perfection of the law, and its fulfillment are the two precepts of charity, how strange is it that he who was forty years minus two was sick? 7. Let us now contemplate the mystery of the healing of this sick person by the Lord. The Lord Himself, the Master of charity, the Fullness of charity, the abbreviated Word arrives upon the earth, as was predicted of Him, and shows that the Law and the Prophets are included in the two precepts of charity. In them, then, Moses is included with his forty number, and Elijah with his, and the Lord used this same number as proof of himself. This sick person is healed by the Savior himself in person. What question do you ask first? Do you want, he says, for me to restore your health? He answers that he doesn't have a man to take him down to the pool. How true it is that she needed a man for her healing!; but it has to be a man who is God too. There is only one God, there is only one mediator between God and men, who is the man Christ Jesus. How then? Becoming equal to God. We all call upon God: Our Father, who art in heaven. It is read that the Jews also said: You are our Father. They were not angry because he said that God was his Father, but because he called him Father in a very different way than men say it. See how the Jews see what the Arians do not want to see. The Arians say that the Son is not equal to the Father, and hence the heresy that afflicts the Church. See how even the blind men and those who killed Christ understood, however, the meaning of Christ's words. They did not see that He was Christ nor that He was the Son of God; but, despite that, they saw in those words such a recommendation of the Son of God, that he had to be equal to God. They did not know who he was, but they saw that he exalted himself to the point of saying that God was his Father, making himself equal to God. So, wasn't he equal to God? It was not He who made Himself equal to God. It was God who had begotten Him equal to Him. If He had made Himself equal to God, this usurpation would have caused Him to fall; Well, he who wanted to make himself equal to God, although he was not, fell, and became an angel and became a devil and gave man this pride to drink, which was what brought him down. What he, already fallen, said to the man, who was still standing, out of the envy he had of him, was this: Taste and you will be like gods. This is: Usurp what you are not, for I also fell by usurpation. He did not say this so clearly, but this is what he implied. Christ, on the other hand, had not become equal to the Father; He had been born from the very substance of the Father; That is why the Apostle makes this recommendation of Him: He who had the form of God was not judged to be equal to God by usurpation. What does it mean that he did not judge it usurpation? That he did not usurp his equality with God, but rather he already had the equality with which he was born. How will one reach Him who is equal to God? He emptied himself by taking the form of a servant. He did not annihilate himself, therefore, by losing what he was, but by taking what he was not.

1. John the Evangelist, among his consorts and co-participants, the other evangelists, receives from the Lord (on whose chest he was reclining at supper, to indicate that he drank the deepest secrets of the inmost depths of his heart) this peculiar gift of his own to reveal such things of the Son of God, which may perhaps awaken the attention of the souls of the little ones, not satisfy them, since they are not capable of it. However, to the souls that are already more grown up and that are internally reaching virile age, he shows in these words something in which to exercise and with which to nourish themselves. You have already heard the reading and you also remember the occasion of this speech. Well, yesterday it was read that the Jews wanted to kill Jesus, not only because he violated the Sabbath, but also because he said that his Father was God and that he was equal to God. What offended the Jews was very pleasing to the Father, as it is also to those who honor the Son with equal honors as the Father; because, if this were not very pleasing to them, they would displease the Father. God is not greater because he is pleasing to you, but you are lesser if he is not pleasing to you. Against this slander, whose origin is evil or ignorance, the Lord says something that they do not fully understand, but enough to stir and disturb them, and perhaps to make them seek the doctor in their confusion. What he said had to be recorded in writing so that we could also read it later. We have already seen the impression that was produced in the hearts of the Jews when they heard these words. Now reflect more carefully on the impression they make on us when we hear them. The heresies and dogmas of perversion, which entangle souls and throw them into the abyss, originate only from the poor understanding of the good Scriptures and from what has been misunderstood being asserted with recklessness and audacity. And so, dearest ones, we must listen with great prudence and with a pious heart and full of holy fear, as Scripture reminds us, everything

And I, brothers, who have set myself the task of speaking to you, want you to think about who I am and what is the task that I have set for myself: I, who am a man, have set myself the task of dealing with divine things; I, who am carnal, deal with spiritual things, and I, who am mortal, deal with things that are eternal. Far be it from me if I want to conduct myself with wisdom within the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. What, according to my ability, I understand, that is what I put on the table for you; When it is shown to me, I feed with you, and when it is hidden from me, I call with you. 2. The Jews are therefore irritated and filled with indignation; and with reason it seems, since a man had the audacity to make himself equal to God; and at the same time, without reason, precisely because they did not see God in that man. They saw the flesh, they did not see God; They saw the room, they did not see the one who inhabits it. That flesh was a temple: God lived inside. Jesus, then, did not establish equality between his flesh and the Father; He did not compare his form as a servant with the Lord, not what he did for us, but what he was when he made us. Who, then, is Christ, you know; You are Catholics, you have the true faith: Christ is neither the Word nor the flesh, but the Word made flesh to live with us. I am going to repeat what you already know about the Word: In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God. See here the equality with the Father. But the Word became flesh and dwelt among us; the Father is greater than this flesh. So the Father is equal and greater: he is equal to the Word and greater than the flesh. Equal to him for whom he made us and greater than he who was made for us.

According to this healthy Catholic rule, which you must first of all know and firmly maintain, those of you who already know it, from which your faith must not slip and no human reasoning must be torn from your heart; According to this rule, I say, we have to measure what we understand. You admitted with me that through the Word everything was made. And now, with carnal and childish feeling, you imagine God working and the Son looking at what the Father does and then He does the same thing too. What does God do without the Word? Because, if he does something, he no longer does it all through the Word and what you stated is false. Now, if it is true that everything was done by the Word, you have to correct your false intelligence. The Father has made all things, but he has not done them except through the Word: how can the Word be looking in order to see the Father do without the Word what the Word is to do in the same way? Everything the Father does, he does through the Word, or it is false that everything was done through Him. But it is true that everything was done through Him. Does that perhaps seem too little to you? And without Him nothing was made. 6. Stop, then, thinking according to the prudence of the flesh and proceed to investigate the meaning of these words: The Son cannot do anything by himself, except what he sees the Father doing. Let us investigate to see if we are worthy of understanding it. I begin, then, by confessing that nothing is greater or more difficult than seeing the Father work for the Son; not the Father and the Son each doing their work, but the Father doing whatever it is for the Son, in such a way that nothing is done for the Father without the Son, nor for the Son without the Father, since everything was done by the Son, and without Him nothing was done. Having established this first on the foundation of faith, how can we now explain that the Son can do nothing by himself, except what he sees the Father doing? You, in my opinion, try to know how the Son works; but the first thing you must know is how the Son sees. What, in fact, does our Lord say? The Son cannot do anything for himself, but what he sees the Father do. Look at what he says: But what he sees the Father do. First the vision and then the action. So go to do. Why do you try to know how he acts, when you still don't know how he sees? Why do you run to what is after, leaving behind what is before? It says that He sees and works, not that He works and sees: He cannot do anything by Himself, except what He sees His Father doing. Do you want me to explain how it works? Explain to me first how he sees. If you can't explain this. I can't give you an explanation for that either.

Put the earthly things on the ground and the heart up. 7. What to do, then, dearest ones? Will I be able to answer these my questions: How does the Word see, and how does the Word see the Father, and what is the seeing of the Word? I am neither so bold nor so reckless that I promise to give myself and you an explanation of this. I may think about your capacity whatever, but I know mine well. If it's okay with you, let's not continue with this any longer; Let us go through the lesson and see how the words of the Lord cast turmoil into carnal hearts and how the turmoil is intended to prevent them from continuing to think as they once thought. Take them away by force, like children, I don't know what games with which they are badly distracted, so that they can be taught in more useful things, like grown-ups, so that they can rise from the earth, on which they walked like reptiles. Arise, and seek, and sigh, and ardently long, and knock at the door that you find closed; For if we still do not desire, nor yearn, nor sigh, we will throw pearls at anyone's feet or we ourselves will find nothing but any pearls. May I, then, see this desire in your hearts, dear ones! Virtue leads to intelligence; The way of living transforms the quality of life. One is earthly life, and another is heavenly life. One is the life of animals, and another is the life of men, and quite another is the life of angels.

The life of beasts burns with desire for the pleasures of the earth; It is the only thing he seeks, it is the only thing he leans towards and gives himself over to. The life of angels is all celestial; The life of men is intermediate between the life of beasts and the life of angels. When man lives according to the flesh, he resembles the beasts.

other hand? The hand certainly makes the same letters, but not in the same way; the heart makes them in an intelligible way, and the hand, in a visible way. See how the same thing is done in a different way. That is why it was not enough for the Lord to say: Everything that the Father does, the Son also does, if he did not add: And in the same way. Because you could understand it this way: Everything the heart does, the hand also does, but in a different way. But here he added: The Son also does them in the same way. Therefore, if he does the same things and in the same way, it is evident (and let the Jew bite his tongue, and let the Christian believe, and let the heretic be convinced) that the Son is equal to the Father. 9. The Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does. Look at this expression: It shows him. Like who? As he who sees. Here I am again involved in what I cannot explain: how the Word sees. Behold, man was made by the Word, and man has eyes, and he has ears, and he has hands, and he has different members in his body. Through his eyes he can see, and through his ears he can hear, and through his hands he can act, and each member has a different function. One member cannot do what another can; However, due to the unity of the body, the eye sees for itself and for the ear, as the ear hears for itself and for the eye. Should something similar be put in the Word for the reason that everything was made by Him? The Scripture says in a psalm: Fools of the people, understand, and you who are foolish, begin to be wise sometime. He who made an ear, will he not hear? Will he who made the eye not see? Yes, then, the Word made the eye, since everything was made by the Word, and if the Word made the hearing, because the Word made everything, it cannot be said: The Word does not hear, the Word does not see, lest the psalm censure us: Fools, begin to be wise sometime. Therefore, if the Word hears and the Word sees, the Son hears and the Son sees. However, should we look for a place for the eyes in the Word other than the place for the ears? Do you hear in one place and see in another1, and your ear cannot exercise the function of the eye nor can the eye exercise the function of your hearing? Or is He all sight and all hearing? Maybe yes; better said, yes, without maybe, because it really is like that; but as long as their seeing and hearing are completely different from our seeing and hearing. Seeing and hearing in the Word are the same. There it is not one thing to hear and another to see, but the hearing is the sight and the sight is the hearing. 10.

How do we know that, since for us hearing is a very different thing from seeing? Perhaps we return to the heart if we are not like those prevaricators of whom it was said: Return, prevaricators, to the heart. Return to the heart. What is this about going away from you and disappearing from your sight?

What is this about going down the paths of solitude and a wandering and wandering life? Come back. Where to? To the Lord. It's still early. Return first to your heart; As in exile you wander outside of yourself. Do you ignore yourself and go in search of the one who created you? Come back, come back to the heart and leave your body; your body is your home. Your heart also feels for your body; but your body doesn't feel what your heart does. Also leave your body and return to your heart. In your body you saw the eyes in one part and the ears in another. Do you see this in your heart? Don't you, perchance, have ears in your heart? Of whom then does the Lord say: He who has ears to hear, let him hear? Don't you have eyes in your heart either? Whence does the Apostle say: The illuminated eyes of your heart? Return to the heart; See there what you perhaps feel about God: there is the image of God. Christ dwells in the inner man, and in the inner man you will be renewed according to the image of God; He knows his Creator in his image. See how all the bodily senses transmit to the heart center the impression they receive from outside! Look how many ministers a single interior emperor has and what he does to himself without these assistants! The eyes give an account to the heart of what is white and what is black, and the ears, what is harmonious and discordant; and the sense of smell, of healthy and fetid odors; and the taste, of the bitter and the sweet; and the touch, of the soft and the rough. And the heart also realizes what is just and what is unjust. Your heart sees and hears and judges of other sensitive people; and where the senses cannot reach, he discerns the just from the unjust and the good from the bad. Show me the eyes, and the ears, and the nostrils of your heart. Various are the impressions that are received in your heart; However, there are no distinct organs there. In your body you hear here and see there; but in your heart you see right there where you hear. If the image can do this, how much more powerful will be the One whose image it is? Therefore the Son hears and the Son sees, and the Son is the same vision and hearing, and in Him hearing is the same as being and seeing is the same as being. In you, seeing is not the same as being, because, if you lose your sight, you can continue being; and if you lose your hearing, you can continue to exist too. 11. Haven't we called? Has something awakened in us that leads us to suspect, even slightly, where the light comes from? I believe, brothers, that talking and meditating on these things is exercising ourselves.

It is certainly about those who were previously half blind) and begin to regain their sight due to the diligence of the doctors. And if the doctor wants to experience the degree of their healing, he tries to show them what they wanted to see and could not, because they were half blind. And, having already recovered their sight to some degree, they are placed in the presence of the light, and when they look at it, they are repelled, in a certain way, by its very brilliance, and they respond to the doctor who is showing it to them: I have seen it with the rapidity of lightning, but I cannot resist the vision. So what does the doctor do? He returns to what he is used to and applies the eye drops so that the desire to see what he saw and could not continue seeing grows, and with this desire he cures him perfectly. And if he has to apply harsh means to obtain this result, he bravely endures them, until he says to himself, enkindled in the love of that light: When will I see with healthy eyes that light that I could not see with wounded and sick eyes? He himself rushes to the doctor and begs him to cure him as soon as possible. Then, brothers, if something similar has happened in your heart, if, however it may be, it has risen from your heart until you see the Word, but, repelled by the brilliance of its light, you have returned to your usual state, ask the doctor to use a more active eye salve, which are the precepts of justice. There are things to see. but there is not what it takes to see them. Before you didn't believe that there were things to see. But, guided by reason, you approached, looked, trembled and turned your eyes. You know, certainly, that there are things to see; but you are not yet able to see them. Heal yourself, then. What are eye drops? Do not lie, and do not perjure, and do not commit adultery, and do not steal, and do not defraud; but, since that is already your habit, you have to leave it with pain; This is what mortifies, but heals. I have spoken to you frankly out of fear, both yours and mine. If you stop healing yourself and despise becoming able to enjoy this light that is the health of your eyes, you will love darkness; If you love darkness, you will remain in it, and if you remain in it, you will also be thrown into the outer darkness, and there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. If the love of light makes no impression on you, let at least the fear of pain make one. 12. In my opinion, I have already been speaking enough, and yet I have not concluded the evangelical lesson.

But, if I continue, I will tire you, and I fear that what has been drunk will not be thrown out; So this is enough for your charity. I owe myself to you now and always as long as I live; I live for you. Serve me, however, as a consolation in this world with your holy life in this my sick and laborious and full life.

It would be enough, then, to say: The hour is coming, and now is when the dead will hear the voice of God (since it is already implied that they will live), whereas, if they did not live, they would not be able to hear it. It does not say: Because they live, they hear; but: Because they hear, they will be quickened; and those who hear it will live. What does it mean then, they will hear, except that they will obey? As for the outer ear, not all who hear live, for many hear and do not believe. If you hear and do not believe, you do not obey; and if you don't obey, you don't live. So hearing means nothing else but obeying. Then those who obey will live; They may be very safe and certain that they will live. Christ is the Word of God and the Son of God, by whom everything was made; who, by divine providence, assumes the flesh and is born of a virgin, and is an infant in the flesh and a youth in the flesh, and suffers in the flesh and dies in the flesh, and rises in the flesh and ascends in the flesh, and promises the resurrection of the flesh; It promises the resurrection of the soul before that of the flesh, and that of the flesh after that of the soul.

He who hears and obeys will live; He who hears and does not obey, that is, he who hears and despises, he who hears and does not believe, will not live. Why doesn't he live? Because he doesn't hear. What is it not to hear? Not obeying; then those who hear will live.

11. Pay attention now to what I decided to defer to see if light is now shed on it. The Lord immediately added about this resurrection: For as the Father has life in himself, so he has given the Son to have life in himself. What does it mean that the Father has life in Himself? That he does not have it in anything else but in himself. Since his life is in Him, it does not come to him from another place; It is not something foreign to Him; He does not have it as a loan or as a participation in a life other than what He is, but rather He has it in Himself, in such a way that He is His own Life. If I can clarify this even more by means of examples to instruct your intelligence, I will do so with the help of God and with the mercy of your intention. God lives, and the soul lives too; but the life of God is immutable, the life of the soul is changeable. God neither grows in perfection nor can lose it; God is always the same in himself: he is as he is; not now in one way, and then in another, and before in another. The life of the soul, on the other hand, is in very different ways. His life yesterday was foolish and today it is wise; Yesterday it was wicked and today it is just; He now remembers and now he forgets, and now he learns and now he cannot learn, and now he experiences the loss of what he had learned and now he knows again what had perished. How changeable is the life of the soul! When the soul lives in iniquity, it is dead; but, when it becomes just, it becomes a participant in another life that is not what it is; because, rising to God and uniting himself to Him, he receives justice from Him, as it is written: He who believes in him who justifies the wicked, his faith justifies him. The same thing that becomes wicked by distancing itself from God, becomes righteous when it approaches Him. Don't you see how something that is cold heats up if it approaches the fire and how it freezes if it withdraws from it? You don't. Do you see how what is in darkness, if it approaches the light, becomes clear, and how, if it is removed from the light, it remains enveloped in darkness? That's right e: soul; God is not like that. I was talking a moment ago about the soul. The soul is even if it is not wise or just; the soul is, and the same, although it is not pious. It is one thing for her to be a soul, and another to be wise, just and holy. It is, therefore, something that does not yet make it wise, nor just, nor pious; However, she is not nothing nor is she without any life: some of her works show that she lives, although she shows no signs of being wise, pious, or just. Because, if she were not alive, she would not move her body and command her feet to walk and her hands to work, and to look with her eyes and hear with her ears, she would not open her mouth to speak or move her tongue to articulate words with distinction. These works show that she lives and that she is something of a better quality than the body. But do these works also show that she is wise, and just, and pious? Or do they not walk, nor act, nor see, nor Do those who are wicked, impious, and unjust hear and speak? But when she takes flight to what she is not, and which is above her, and from whom she receives her being, then she perceives wisdom, and justice, and piety, without which, even when she existed, she was dead, she did not have the life with which she lives, but only the life with which she gives life to the body.

It is one thing in the soul that gives life to the body, and another thing is what gives life to itself. It is better, of course, than the body, but better than it is God. She is, although foolish, and unjust, and impious, the life of the body. God is your life. And just as, when it is in the body, it communicates vigor, and strength, and movement.

You are the Son of man. You, yes, will be present at the judgment, and the bodies will be resurrected; tell us something about the trial, this PS. of discernment between the good and the bad. Hear also this: And those who did good will rise to life, and those who did evil will rise through judgment. When you previously spoke of the resurrection of spirits and souls, did you establish any distinction? No, • but: All those who hear will live, because by obeying they will have life. But at the resurrection and exit from the tombs, not everyone will go to eternal life, but only those who did good, and, on the other hand, those who did evil will go to judgment. Here the word judgment means punishment. There will then be separation, but not like now. For now we are also separated from each other, but not by place, but by customs, and by affection, and by desires, and by faith, and by hope, and by charity. Now we are mixed in life with the wicked, but not everyone's life is the same. The separation, the division, is hidden; something like grain on the threshing floor, not like grain in the barn. The separation is made on the threshing floor, but the mixture still remains; The separation is made when the grain is stripped from the chaff, but the mixture still remains, because the fork has not yet been made. Then there will be manifest separation: as in customs, so in life also; As in wisdom, so in bodies. Those who did good will go to live with the angels of God; On the contrary, those who did evil will go to be tortured with the devil and his angels. And the servant form will go from there too. That form was present there to judge. After the judgment he will leave there and take with him the body of the one who is the head and will offer the kingdom to God. It is then that that form of God that could not be seen by the wicked will be seen with complete clarity, to whose sight alone the form of a servant was to be presented. In another place it also says this: These (those on the left) will go to eternal fire; but the righteous, to eternal life. Of which he speaks thus in another place: This is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you sent. Then the same one will be revealed there who, having the form of God, did not believe his equality with God to be a plunder. Then he will show himself, as he promised to show himself to his lovers.

Return, then, to what I was saying, because perhaps that is the true way to understand it, to get both of us out of the proposed difficulty. Of course, according to the Catholic faith, I see the way out without harm and without any stumbling blocks; but you, closed in everywhere, are looking for the exit. You have to first see where you came in. Maybe you haven't realized what I just told you: to first look at where you came in. Listen to Him Himself, who says: I am the door. It is not without reason that you are looking for the exit and you cannot find it, because you did not enter through the door, but rather you fell over the wall. You have to recover from your disaster as best you can and enter through the door, so that you don't get hurt and leave without getting lost. Enter through Christ and do not say what your heart inspires you, but what He makes known to you. That's what you have to say. Now look how the Catholic faith emerges from this difficulty: the Son walked on the waters and placed his plants of flesh on them; The flesh walked and the divinity ruled it, was the Father absent? If He was absent, how is it that the Son Himself says: The Father, who abides in me, Himself does His works? Therefore, if the Father remains in the Son, and He Himself does His works, that walk of the flesh on the waves of the sea was done by the Father; through the Son he did it. Therefore that walk is the inseparable work of the Father and the Son: I am seeing both of them working there. Neither the Father leaves the Son alone nor does the Son distance himself from the Father; and thus everything that the Son does, he does not do it without the Father, because everything that the Father does he does not do without the Son. 7. This is our Teacher so that we do not sin, and he is our Advocate if, after having sinned, we confess and return to Him, and he is our intercessor if we want to obtain something good from the Lord, and our Benefactor with the Father, because the Father - and the Son are one God. But he said all these things to men as a man; hidden like God and visible like man, to make gods of those who were evidently men; and he who was the Son of God became the Son of man in order to make children of God those who were children of men. What art he used his infinite wisdom to accomplish this, can be seen from his words. He speaks as small to those who are small, and he is such a small person, who is also great. We, however, are small, but in Him we are great; He speaks, then, as one who caresses and nourishes infants who are growing in love. 2. The Lord had said: The Son cannot do anything by himself except what he sees the Father doing. We understood that the Father does not carry out works separately in order for the Son to see them and do similar works looking at the works of his Father. These words: The Son cannot of himself do anything except what he sees the Father doing, mean that the Son is all of the Father and that all his substance and power is of him who begot him. But now, next to stating that He performs in the same way the works that the Father performs, so that it is not understood that the Father does some works and the Son other works, but rather that, by virtue of the same power, He does the same as the Father, since the Father works for the Son, he continues and says what has been heard read today: The Father loves the Son and shows him everything that He does. New disturbance in the thinking of the mor. such. The Father shows the Son what He accomplishes; then, someone will say, the Father does some work separately, in order that the Son can see what he does. Once again the occurrence of two architects comes to human thought. Something like if an artist taught his son his art and showed him everything he does so he could do it too. It shows him, he says, everything He does.

Therefore, when the Father works, does not the Son work so that the Son can see what the Father does? Is it not true that everything was made by the Son and without Him nothing was made? Here we see in what sense it is said that the Father shows the Son what He did. Aug. 13

No matter how much, then, we understand and how much we see, and even if we were equal to the angels in this, we will never see to the degree in which the Son sees. Because we are something even in the moments when we do not see. What are we when we do not see, but men who do not see? Therefore we exist even if we do not see; and to see we turn to the one we want to see, and the vision that did not exist when we already existed is realized. There is, then, the man who does not see; and that same man, when he can see, is called a seeing man. In man it is not the same thing to see as to be a man; because, if seeing were the same as being a man, there would never be a man who was not always seeing. And since there is a man who does not see and who pretends to see what he does not see, that man is a subject who seeks and a subject who turns to see. And when he has turned and has managed to see, it is the name that the same man who previously was a man who did not see sees. Vision, then, is something that comes to him and leaves him: it comes to him when he turns to the objects and leaves him when he moves away. Is the Son like this? By no means. He was never a Son who did not see and then came to see, but seeing the Father is the same as being a Son. We, going after sin, lost the light, and with our return to God we receive the light. The light that illuminates us is one thing and we, who are illuminated, are another. The Light, which illuminates us, does not move away from itself nor does it lose its radiance, because it is the light itself. This is how the Father shows the Son the works that he does, in the sense that the Son sees all things in the Father, and so is the Son all things in the Father. Then seeing he was born and being born he sees. He was never unborn and then born; as He was never without seeing and then saw, but in Him seeing is the same as existing, and being born, and lasting in existence, and being immutable, and continuing to exist without beginning and without end.

Therefore, it should not be carnally understood that the Father sits down and performs a work and then shows it to the Son, and then the Son sees what the Father has done and then does another similar thing in another space or of another matter. The one who speaks to us is God and he is man, we discern the words of God and the words of man. Because there are times when he tells us things that belong to majesty, and other times he tells us things that belong to his state of humiliation. The same one who is humble is exalted to make us exalted, who are humble. What then are his words? The Father will show me greater works than these, so that you may be filled with amazement. Therefore it is to us that He is going to show them, not to Him. And since it is to us that He is going to show them to us, that is why He adds: So that you may be filled with amazement. He explained what these words mean: The Father will show me. Why did he not say: The Father will show you, but: The Father will show the Son? It is that we are members of the Son; and what we, his members, learn, he learns in a certain way in his members. How does he learn in us? How does it suffer in us? How can we jjrobar what suffers in us? By that voice that was heard from heaven: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? Is he not the same one who will sit as a judge at the end of the ages and will place the righteous on his right and the wicked on his left and will pronounce this sentence: Come, you who are blessed by my Father, and possess the kingdom, because I was hungry and you gave me food? And to their question: Lord, when did we see you hungry?, he will answer like this: When you gave something to one of these little ones, you gave it to me. To the same man, then, who gave this answer: When you gave something to one of these little ones, you gave it to me, let us now ask him this question, saying: Lord, when will you be a disciple, you who teach all things? He will give us the answer instantly according to the principles of our faith: When one of my little ones learns, I learn too. 8. Let us therefore congratulate ourselves and be grateful; we have been made to become not only Christians, but Christ himself. Do you realize, brothers, do you understand what God has done to us? It is so that you are filled with admiration and joy. We have been made to become Christ himself. For, if He is the head and we are the members, the whole man is He and we. This is what the apostle Paul affirms: In order that we may no longer be children, who are carried and brought about by all the winds of doctrine.

Previously he had already said: Until we all reach the unity of faith and knowledge of the Son of God, to the age of perfect man, to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ. There is, without a doubt, a true and powerful thought (if we can somehow find it) in these words: The Father judges no one, but gave all judgment to the Son. This is said because in the judgment only the Son will be shown to men. The Father will not become visible; the Son, yes. What will be visible in the Son? The way it went up. The form of God is hidden with the Father; the slave form is the one that will become visible to men. The Father, therefore, does not judge anyone, but gave all the power to judge to the Son, but to judge publicly or visibly. In this visible judgment the Son will judge, because He is the one who will appear to those who are to be judged. Scripture tells us clearly that He will become visible. Forty days after his resurrection he ascended to heaven in the sight of his disciples; and an angel said to them: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking at heaven? This same one who, leaving you, went to heaven, will return in the same way that you saw him ascend to heaven. How did you see him going up? With the same flesh that they touched and felt, and of whose scars they were also convinced by touching them, and, with the same body that, for forty days, came in and out with them, making itself visible to them in its true reality, not in some appearance or falsehood, like a ghost, or a shadow, or a spirit, but, as He Himself said, not leading them to err: Feel and see that the spirit has neither flesh nor bones, as you are seeing that I have. That body, in truth, is already worthy of the heavenly abode: it is not subject to death nor is it subject to the change of ages. The age of Christ's youth, which he reached by growing from childhood, no longer knows decline, no longer reaches old age, but remains eternally as he ascended, and thus he must return to those to whom, before returning, he wanted his Gospel to be preached. He will come, then, like this, in human form. The wicked will see it, and those on the right will see it, and those on the left will see it; This is how it is written: They will see him whom they pierced. If they will see the one they pierced, they will see the very body that they pierced with the spear: the spear does not hurt the Word. The wicked will only be able to see what they were able to hurt. They will not see the God hidden in the flesh.

You did not say: They will go to see me in the form of God and they will go to see the Father, to whom I am equal. And now, then, following the aforementioned judgment, everything being referred to the Son, since the Father judges no one, what will happen? What's next? So that everyone honors the Son, as they honor the Father. The Jews honor the Father and despise the Son. The Son was looked upon as a servant and the Father was honored as God. The Son will also show himself to be equal to the Father, so that everyone will honor the Son as they honor the Father. Now we know this by faith. Let the Jew not come saying: I honor the Father, and with the Son, what have I to do? Reply to him: He who does not honor the Son, does not honor the Father either. You lie completely; blasphemes of Christ and insults the Father. The Father sent the Son, and you despise his sent. That the Son is lesser because it is said that he is sent? Mission is what I hear, not separation.

The Lord our God himself is the one who reveals and teaches us through his Scriptures the meaning of the word judgment. I urge you, therefore, to be attentive. The word judgment sometimes means punishment and other times discernment or discrimination. If it is taken as discernment, then, yes, we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that there man may receive the good or evil that he accomplished through the body. True discernment is giving good to good and evil to bad. Because, if judgment always means something bad, the Psalm would never say: Judge me, O God! Perhaps you hear someone say: Judge me, oh God!, and you are surprised. Because man usually says: Forgive me, Lord. Forgive me, oh God! But who is there that says: Judge me, O God? And sometimes this verse is placed in a place where the song is alternate; The reader recites it and the people repeat it. Is it not true that one is deeply impressed and fears to address this song to God, saying: Judge me, O God? The faithful people, however, sing it and do not believe that what they learned in the divine lesson is an evil desire. And if you don't quite understand the meaning, believe, nevertheless, that there is something good in it. The psalm itself explains its meaning to us. Next, he shows what judgment he is talking about, which is not a judgment of condemnation, but discrimination. Because he says: 'Judge me, O God! What does it mean: Judge me, O God! And discriminate my cause from that of these evil people? According to this judgment of discrimination, we all have to appear before the judgment seat of Christ.

If, on the contrary, it is a question of the judgment of condemnation: He who hears my word, says, and believes in him who sent me, has eternal life and will not stand in judgment, but "passes from death to life. What does it mean: Will not stand in judgment? That he will not incur condemnation. I am going to prove from the Scriptures that the word judgment sometimes has the meaning of punishment. The Apostle says in one place, writing to those who desecrated the body, which you, as faithful, know, and for desecrating it were punished by the Lord; That is why there are many among you who are sick and weak and many who die. Many, it is true, also died for that. The Apostle continues speaking: If we judged ourselves, we would not be judged by the Lord; That is, if we corrected ourselves, we would not be punished by the Lord. But, when we are punished, we are corrected by the Lord, so as not to be condemned with this world. There are, then, those who are punished here in order to be forgiven there; there is. others who are treated leniently here in order to be punished more harshly there; and there are others, finally, to whom punishments that do not have the character of a scourge are inflicted here and there, if they have refused to correct themselves with divine punishments; so that, because they have despised the father's whippings here, they have to feel there the hard hand of the Judge, who punishes. Then there is a judgment to which God, that is, the Son of God, will urge the devil and his angels and all the impious and unfaithful with Him to appear at the end of the world. Because he is the Son of God, as the Father has life in himself, he also gave the Son to have life in himself; and because he was the Son of man, he gave him the power to judge. It is the same thing that I explained to your charity yesterday: that in the judgment it is the man who will be seen, but God will not be seen. And because man will be seen in the judgment in that same form in which he will come as he came, that is why he said before: The Father does not judge anyone, but gave all judgment to the Son. This is what he repeats and says in this place: He gave him the power to judge because he is the Son of man. As if you said: Did he give him the power to judge? Because? When did you not have this power to judge? When in the beginning the Word existed, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God, and when everything was made by Him, did He not have the power to judge? Let us raise it, then, with its help; it weighs a lot. Why is it heavy? For the corruptible body greatly oppresses the soul, and this terrestrial habitation depresses the soul divided into many thoughts. Perhaps we cannot isolate our spirit from so much confusion of things and, thus isolated, collect it and fix it in one (we cannot do this, I have already said, without the help of him whose will is that our souls should be elevated to Him), nor understand in any way how the Word of God, the Only Begotten of the Father, coeternal and equal to the Father, does only what he sees the Father doing, whereas the Father does nothing either except for the Son, who is seeing what he sees. ago. It seems to me that the will of the Lord Jesus in this passage is to insinuate something great to the well-disposed and to instill it in those already qualified and to excite those who do not yet have the capacity to study, so that, seeing that they do not understand it, they may be able to train themselves by living well. It teaches us, therefore, that the human soul and the rational mind, which man possesses and not brutes, cannot receive life, nor happiness, nor* light, except from the very substance of God. This soul can act through the body and, with the help of the body, have the body subdued; and through corporeal things the senses can receive pleasant or unpleasant impressions, and through this, that is, through the consortium and union of the soul and the body in this life, the alnuí receives joy or sadness, according to the softness or harshness of the impressions of the senses. The blessedness, however, of the soul, by which it is happy, is not achieved except by the participation of that life which is always alive and which is immutable and eternal substance; that is, from God. And just as the soul, which is inferior to God, communicates life to what is inferior to it, that is, to the body, in the same way the same soul cannot receive the life that makes it happy except from what is superior to the soul itself. The soul is superior to the body, and God is superior to the soul. The soul gives something to the lower, and it receives it from the higher.

Let's ask the miracles themselves what they tell us about Christ, since they also have their language, but it is as long as it is understood; for as Christ himself is the Word of God, so also the acts of the Word are words for us. Then, just as we have heard the greatness of this miracle, let us also investigate its great depth. Let us not be content with merely superficial delight; Let us deepen its perfect sublimity. That same thing that causes our admiration from the outside, contains something inside. We have seen, we have contemplated something great, something excellent, something that is entirely divine and that only God can achieve; and by the work we have burst forth in praise of its Maker. But just as, if we saw beautifully made letters in a codex, we would not be satisfied with the mere praise of the perfection of the hand of the writer who made them so similar, equal and beautiful, if we did not come to understand, through reading, what he wanted to tell us in them, the same thing happens here: those who only look at this fact from the outside are delighted by its beauty to the point of admiration of the craftsman; but he who understands it is like he who reads. A painting is viewed differently from writing. Thus, when you see a painting, you have already seen everything, you have already praised everything; On the other hand, when you see a scripture, it is not the whole thing to see; the scripture itself is urging you to read it. You yourself, too, when you see a piece of writing and perhaps you don't know how to read it, you express yourself like this: What could he have written here? You ask about what is written, since you already see the writing. The one from whom you ask for an explanation of what you have seen is going to show you something very different. - He has some eyes and you have others. Don't you both see the writing equally? What is it composed of? What is it formed from? From the number five. The number five symbolizes the law. There are five books of Moses, and five are the porches in which the sick lie, and five are the loaves that feed five thousand men. This Son of man, chosen by a singular grace of the Spirit and Son of man according to the flesh, despite being an exception among men, is the Son of man. This Son of man is also the Son of God; This man is God too. In another place he asks the disciples this question: Who do men say the Son of Man is? They answer: Some say that John, others that Elijah, others that Jeremiah or another of the ancient prophets. And he continues asking: And you, who do you say I am? Peter gives this answer: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. He is called the Son of man, and Peter calls him the Son of the living God. He spoke very accurately about what was out of mercy for everyone to see; Peter spoke of what remains in the radiance of his glory. The Word of God recommends your humility; man realizes the radiance of the glory of his Lord. And truly, brothers, I think this is just. He humbled Himself for us, let us glorify Him. Not because of Him is the Son of Man, but because of us. Therefore he was the Son of man in this sense, since the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Therefore, God-Father put his seal on it. What is sealing but putting something of your own? To seal is to put a sign on something so that it is distinguished from the rest. To seal is to put a sign on a thing. What works do you do? Was it not enough to have eaten your fill with only five loaves? They knew this, but they valued the manna from heaven more than this food. They observed that he promised more, but they were blindfolded so as not to see that he was doing greater works. Look, look carefully and consider it well: He who comes to me I will not cast out. Therefore whoever comes to me, he says, I will not cast him out. Because? It is that I have descended from heaven not to do my will, but the will of the one who sent me. Is the reason why you do not cast out anyone who comes to you because you came down from heaven not to do your will, but the will of the one who sent you? Yes, that's the reason. Why do we look for whether that is the reason or not? The reason is; He says it himself. It is not permissible for us to think of any other reason than the one He gives: He who comes to me I will not throw away; and as if you were looking for the reason, he answers: Because I have not come from heaven to do my will, but the will of the one who sent me. I fear that the reason the soul leaves God is because it is pride; rather, I do not even doubt it, since it is written: The beginning of all sin is pride; and also: The beginning of man's pride is separation from God. This is what is written, this is immutable, this is true. Furthermore, what does Scripture say to the proud mortal, covered with the rags of the flesh and oppressed by the weight of corruptible flesh and who, nevertheless, takes pride and forgets the covering that covers him? What does Scripture tell you? What can he who is earth and ashes be proud of? What can you be proud of? Let him say it: Because in his life he threw his most intimate part. What does it mean to throw, but to throw away? This is what is called going outside. To enter what is most interior is to desire what is most intimate, and to throw away the most intimate intimacies is to go outside. Through pride we go outside, through humility we return inside. 16. My feet, he says, were already sliding. Because? Out of envy of the wicked, contemplating their peace. Then to whom is God good but to the upright in heart? For I, who have a crooked heart, did not please God. Why didn't you like it? Because he made the bad guys happy; and that is why my feet wavered, as if my services to God were in vain... That is precisely why my feet were on the verge of slipping, because I was not upright in heart. So what does it mean to be upright in heart? That fulfills the will of God. The one is happy; the other suffers; This one lives badly and is happy; the one lives according to justice and suffers. Let not he be angry who lives according to justice and suffers; He carries within him what he who is happy does not have. Therefore do not be sad, nor tormented, nor faint. This man who seems happy has gold in his coffers, and this one, on the other hand, has God in his conscience. Now compare gold with God, and chests with conscience. That one has something perishable, and he has it there where it can be stolen. This man, on the other hand, has God, who cannot perish, and he has him there from where no one can take him away, provided he is of upright heart; because then it comes in and doesn't come out. The same one who said: My bones have rejoiced, had begun by saying: You will give my ear joy and gladness. What does it mean to my ear? Just by hearing you I am happy, and with your voice alone I am happy, and drinking from within I am happy. That is why I do not fall, and that is why my bones rejoice, and that is why the friend of the Bridegroom stands tall and is listening: "He stands tall precisely because he is listening." He drinks from the fountain that is within, and that is why he remains standing. Those who refused to drink from the inner fountain fell and were thrown out and could not stand. 18. The Master, therefore, of humility has come, not to do his will, but the will of the one who sent him. Let us come to Him, let us enter into Him and incorporate ourselves into Him so that we do not do our will either, but the will of God. This is how he will not cast us out, because we are his members, since he wanted to be head as a Master of humility. Listen, lastly, to Himself, who speaks: Come to me, all you who are weary and oppressed by the burden, and take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am meek and humble in heart. When you learn this lesson, you will find rest for your souls, from which you will not be cast out: For I have come down from heaven, not to do my will, but the will of him who sent me. I teach humility; Only he who is humble can reach me. Only pride casts out. How will he who maintains humility and remains faithful to the truth be cast out? I have said, brothers, everything I could about the hidden meaning of these words. The meaning is very hidden here and I don't know if I have been able to find it and explain it with adequate words; because he does not cast out anyone who comes to him precisely because he has not come to do his will, but the will of the one who sent him. 19. It is not, therefore, my Father's will that a single one of these little ones perish. Therefore, if I, who am a man, teach him who hears my word, the Father also teaches him who hears his word. If the Father teaches those who hear his word, investigate what Christ is and you will know his Word: In the beginning the Word existed. It does not say that in the beginning God made the Word, as it says that in the beginning God made heaven and earth. The reason is because the Word is not a creature. Learn the way to be drawn to the Son by the Father, may the Father teach you, listen to his Word. Which Verb of yours do you say I listen to? He lives for the Father, who has sent him; because he emptied himself, becoming obedient to the point of death on a cross. If we take these words: I live for the Father, in the same sense as those others: The Father is greater than me, we can also say that we live for Him, because He is greater than us. All this is so by the very fact of being sent. His mission is, certainly, the annihilation of himself and his acceptance of the form of a servant; which can rightly be said, even preserving the absolute identity of nature of the Son with the Father. The Father is greater than the Son-man; but the Father has a SonGod, who is equal to Him, since one and the same is God and man, Son of God and Son of man, who is Christ Jesus. And in this sense he said (if these words are understood correctly): Just as the living Father sent me and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me will live because of me. As if to say: The reason that I live for the Father, that is, that I refer to Him as the greatest of my life, is my annihilation in the one who sent me; but the reason that anyone lives for me is the participation of me when he eats me. Thus I, humbled, live for the Father, and he, exalted, lives for me. If it was said Alive by the Father in the sense that He comes from the Father and not the Father from Him, this was said without any detriment to the identity between the two. But saying: He who eats me will live through me, does not mean identity between Him and us, but simply shows the grace of a mediator. 20. This is the bread that came down from heaven, so that by eating it we might have life, since we cannot have eternal life of ourselves. Not as, he says, your fathers ate manna and died; He who eats this bread will live forever. Those words: They died, mean that they will not live forever. For those who eat Christ will truly die temporarily; but they live eternally, since Christ is eternal life.

1. We have listened carefully through the reading of the gospel to the words of the Lord that follow my previous sermon. Hence the obligation I have to speak to your ears and intelligence, and today is very appropriate. The issue is about the body of the Lord, which he told us was given to us to eat for eternal life. He explains the way to give Himself and His gifts to us; the way of giving us his flesh to eat, saying: Whoever eats my body and drinks my blood is in me and I in him. The sign that someone eats and drinks it is if Christ abides in him and he in Christ; if Christ dwells in him and he dwells in Christ, and if he is united to Him so as not to be abandoned. This teaches us and warns us with words full of mystery: that we be in his body with his members under the head, which is Him, eating his flesh and not separating ourselves from his unity. But many of those present did not understand and were scandalized; When they heard these things, they thought only of the flesh, because that was what was wrong: flesh. The Apostle says, and it is true: To understand according to the flesh is death. The Lord gives us his flesh so that we may eat it, and to understand this according to the flesh is death, whereas He says of his flesh that eternal life is there; Therefore we must not understand the flesh according to the flesh, as is deduced from the following words. 2. Many of those who heard him, not of his enemies, but of his disciples, said: What a harsh speech this is! Who can hear it? If the disciples judged these words to be so harsh, what would their enemies judge of them? However, it was necessary that it be expressed in such a way that not everyone would understand it. God's secrets should excite our attention, not our aversion. These separated from Him immediately, as soon as the Lord Jesus uttered such words. They did not believe the one who said something immense nor the one who hid ineffable graces in his words. They understood them to their liking, certainly very human, namely: That Jesus wanted or that Jesus intended to give to whoever believed in Him the flesh with which the Word was clothed, torn into pieces. How hard, they say, are these words! What ear can bear them?
