Jesus knowing in Himself that His disciples were murmuring about this (they spoke this among themselves, so that He did not want it; but since none of it was hidden from Him, hearing in Himself what they said), he answered and said: Does this offend you, because I said that I give you my flesh to eat and my blood to drink? Is that what scandalizes you? What will it be, then, if you manage to see the Son of Man ascend to where he was first? What does this mean? Does this make what bothered you disappear? Do you discover with this the meaning of what scandalized them? Yes, certainly, as long as they understood it. They believed that he was going to give them his body, and He says that he will ascend to heaven, and certainly all of it. When you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was first, then you will clearly realize that he does not give you his body to eat as you think, then you will certainly realize that his grace is not eaten by bites. 4. And he continued saying: It is the spirit that gives life, but the flesh is of no use. Before explaining this, as the Lord gives us to understand, what he said before should not be overlooked lightly: What will happen then when you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was first? The Son of man, Christ, was born of the Virgin Mary. Then the Son of Man began to exist on the earth at the very moment that he took on flesh, which comes from the earth. Therefore it was prophetically said: Truth was born from the earth. What, then, is the meaning of these words: When you see the Son of man, will he ascend to where he was before? There would be no problem if he had said: If you see the Son of God ascend to where he was before; But, since he said that the Son of man ascended to where he was before, could it be that the Son of man was in heaven when he began to exist on earth? Here he says where he was before, as if back then, when he said these things, he was not there. But in another passage it says: No one ascends into heaven except He who came down from heaven, the Son of man, who is in heaven. It does not say that he was, but it says: the Son of man, who is in heaven. He speaks on earth and says he is in heaven; and it does not say in this way: No one ascends into heaven except He who came down from heaven, the Son of God, who is in heaven.

Why this way of speaking if not so that we understand what I already explained to your charity in a previous sermon: that Christ, God and man, is one person, not two; Is it not going to happen that our faith has as its object not a trinity, but a quaternity? Therefore Christ is one person; the Word, the soul and the flesh are one Christ; and the Son of man and the Son of God is one Christ. Son of God eternally, Son of man temporally

What is the meaning of the following words: It is the spirit that gives life, but the flesh is of no use? Let us tell him (He allows us this as long as we do not contradict him, but with a desire to learn): Oh Lord, good Teacher! How is it that the flesh is of no use, seeing as you say: Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and if you do not drink his blood, you will have no life in you? Is life useless? Are we not what we are so that we may have eternal life, which you promise us with your flesh? What does it mean that meat is worthless? Meat is worth nothing in the sense in which they understood it: dead meat, cut into pieces or as it is sold in the market, not meat quickened by the spirit. It is said, then, that meat is useless in the same sense that science is said to swell. But is that why you should hate science? No. What does it mean that science swells? When she is alone without charity. That is why he added: Charity edifies. Combine charity with science, and science will be useful, not by itself, but by charity. The same here: Meat is worthless, that is, meat alone; But let the spirit be united with the flesh, as charity is united with science, and then it is worth a lot. Because, if the flesh is worthless, the Word would not have become flesh to live with us. If Christ was worth much to us through his flesh, how is the flesh worthless? The spirit accomplished something for our health through the flesh. Meat is a vessel; Look carefully at what it contains, not what it is. The apostles were sent; Is their flesh worthless to us? If the flesh of the apostles served us for something, is it possible that the flesh of the Lord serves no purpose? Where does the sound of his word come to us if not through the voice of the flesh? Where from the pen and where the writing? All this is done by the flesh, but moved by the spirit as its organ or instrument. The spirit, then, is what gives life, but the flesh is worthless; but it is the flesh as God understood it; I do not feed my meat in this sense. 6. Therefore, he says, the words that I speak to you are spirit and life.

He dwells in us when we are his temple. Unity brings us together so that we can be its members; and unity is brought about by charity. And what is the source of charity? Ask the Apostle: The charity of God, he says, is spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. Therefore it is the Spirit who gives life, because the Spirit is who makes the members have life. The Spirit only gives life to the members that it finds united to the body, which informs and vivifies. For does the spirit that exists in you, O man, and through which you are man, perchance give life to the members that are separated from the body? I call your soul your spirit; and your soul only vivifies the members that are united with your body. If you separate one, it is no longer quickened by your soul, because it is no longer part of the unity of your body. These things are said to make us fall in love with unity and fear division. Nothing should be so fearful to the Christian as separating himself from the body of Christ, because, if he separates himself from the body of Christ, he is no longer a member of it; and if he is not a member of his, he does not live by his Spirit. He who does not have, says the Apostle, the Spirit of Christ, such is not Christ's. The Spirit is, therefore, the one who gives life, the flesh is worthless; The words that I speak to you are spirit and life. What does it mean that they are spirit and life? That must be understood spiritually. Have you understood them spiritually? So they are spirit and life. Have you understood them carnally? Even so understood, they are spirit and life, but they are not for you. 7. But there are some, he says, among you who do not believe. It does not say: There are some among you who do not understand, but it tells the reason why they do not understand. There are some among you who do not believe, and therefore they do not understand, because they do not believe. The prophet already says: If you do not believe, you will not understand. Faith unites us and intelligence vivifies us. Let us constitute ourselves in unity through faith, so that what can be vivified by intelligence may come into existence. Those who do not join, put up resistance; and whoever opposes does not believe. Can he who resists be quickened? It is an enemy of the ray of light, which should penetrate it; He doesn't take his eyes off, but he closes his mind. So there are some who do not believe. Let them believe and open, let them open their intelligence and they will be enlightened. Jesus knew from the beginning who the believers would be and who would hand him over. Well, Judas was also there.

Some were scandalized; but he stayed to lay traps for him, not to understand. And because he stayed with that goal, the Lord spoke of him. He did not name him clearly, but he did not keep silent about him either, in order to instill fear in everyone, even if only one was the one who had joined.

And after saying and distinguishing those who believed from those who did not believe, he made known why they did not believe: That is why I told you, he added, that no one can come to me unless it is given to him by my Father. Therefore believing is also given to us, because believing is something. If, then, it is a great thing, rejoice because you believed, but do not be proud. Well, what do you have that you haven't received? 8. From that moment on, many of his disciples went back and no longer followed him. They turned back, but to go after Satan, not after Christ. On one occasion, the Lord called Peter Satan, because he wanted to go before Him and give him advice that he who had come to death should not die so that we would not all die eternally. And he said to him: Go after me, Satan; You have no taste for the things of God, but for those of men. He did not reject him to go after Satan, and yet he called him Satan. He made him go after Him, after the Lord, so that he would stop being Satan. These retreated in the manner of those women of whom the Apostle says: Some retreated, but to go after Satan. They no longer followed him. This is how, separated from the body, they lost their lives, because, surely, they were never united to the body. They must be counted among those who do not believe, even if they call themselves his disciples. Not a few, but many, stopped going after Him. This surely happened to our comfort. It sometimes happens that a man tells the truth, and his words are not understood, and those who hear them are scandalized and leave. It hurts the man to have told the truth and he reacts like this inside: I shouldn't have spoken like that, I shouldn't have said this. Look, this also happened to the Lord. He spoke and lost many and kept few. But He is not disturbed; He knew from the beginning who would believe and who would not believe. If this happens to us, we are disturbed. Let us take comfort in the Lord and be very careful when we speak. 9. And He addresses the few who had remained with Him. Jesus said to the twelve, that is, to those who remained with Him: Do you also want to flee from my company? No one left, not even Judas. But the Lord already knew why he didn't leave, and we found out later. Peter answers, in the name of all, one for many, unity through universality. So Simon Peter answered: Lord, to whom shall we go? Do you take us away from you? Give us another one just like you. Who will we go to? If we leave your company, who will we go to?

Threshing destroys what cleans the fork, so we are certain, brothers, that all of us who are members of the body of the Lord and remain in Him, in order that He also remain in us, of necessity have to live in this world, until the end of life, mixed with the evil ones. What else does it mean but what the martyrs heard: He who endures to the end will be saved? How did he remain in El San Lorenzo, whose festival we celebrate today? He remained until the test, and until the tyrant's interrogation, and until the most cruel threats, and until death; and this is still little: he remained until the most inhuman torture. They did not kill him with a slash, but rather he was tortured by fire. His life was prolonged; Or rather, his life was not prolonged, but rather he was forced to die more slowly. But in that slow death, in those torments, he did not feel the pain: he had eaten and drank well, he had become stronger and as if intoxicated with that food and that drink. There was present the one who said: The spirit is what gives life. The flesh burned, but the spirit gave life to his soul. He did not surrender, and entered into possession of the kingdom. The holy martyr Sixtus, whose feast we celebrated five days ago today, had said to him: Do not grieve, son. That one was a bishop, and this one a deacon. Do not grieve, he says; After three days you will follow me. The three days are the time between the day of the martyrdom of Saint Sixtus and today, which is the martyrdom of Saint Lawrence. The average time is three days. What great joy! It does not say: Do not grieve, son; The persecution will cease and you will be calm; but: Do not grieve, you will follow me where I go before you; It will not take long for you to follow me: it will only take three days and you will be with me. From this gospel text: "After this Jesus walked through Galilee", to this other: "However, no one spoke openly about Him for fear of the Jews"

1. In this text of the gospel, brothers, our Lord Jesus Christ offers himself very particularly to us as a man. For he always tries by his words and actions to be believed to be God and man: God who made us, man who came in search of us; God always with the Father and man with us temporarily. Because he would not go in search of the man he had made if he did not become the same thing he had made. However, always remember this and may it never be erased from your spirit, namely: Christ became man without ceasing to be God. Remaining God, the same one who made man took on man. When, therefore, he hides himself as a man, let it not be thought that he lost his power, but that he wanted to set an example of weakness. Because He was arrested when He wanted, and when He wanted He was killed. But since His members, that is, His faithful, who would exist in the future, would not have the same power that our God Himself had, by hiding Himself and concealing Himself to avoid having His life taken away, He indicated what His members should do, in which He was certainly present. Because Christ is not only in the head and not in the body, but Christ is entirely in the head and in the body. What his members are, he is also; but what He is is not always what His members are. For, if He Himself were not its members, He had no reason to say: Saul, why do you persecute me? Saul was not persecuting Him on earth, but rather his members, his faithful. He did not mean to say to my saints, to my servants, nor, finally, what is even more honorable, to my brothers, but to me, that is, to my members, of whom I am the head. 2. With these principles established, I believe that the passage that has just been read will not be difficult; It is often said about the head what was going to happen in the body. After this, he says, Jesus was walking in Galilee; He did not want to go to Judea because the Jews were looking for him to kill him. That's what I said: an example of our weakness. He had not lost His power, but consoled our weakness. It would be a fact, as I said, that some of his faithful would hide so that his pursuers would not find him; and

Those who have read the Scriptures know perfectly well what the Feast of Tabernacles is. On the day of the festival the Jews made tents similar to those in which they had lived, after their departure from Egypt, during their pilgrimage through the desert. That was a party of great solemnity. The Jews celebrated this festival as a remembrance of the benefits of the Lord, and it was celebrated by the same people who were to kill the Lord. Well, on this day of the festival (since the festival was several days, and by the Jews the festival was called that way, which was not just one day, but many) their brothers spoke to our Lord Jesus Christ. Understand this about his brothers, as you already know; What you hear is not unknown to you. The relatives of the Virgin Mary were called brothers of the Lord. In fact, it was customary in the Scriptures to give the name of brothers to all those who were united to each other by ties of consanguinity or kinship, contrary to our custom and our way of speaking. Because who calls uncle and sister's son brothers? Scripture, however, calls those who are related to each other brothers. And so Abraham and Lot are called brothers, Abraham being Lot's uncle; and Laban and Jacob the same, Laban being Jacob's paternal uncle. Then, when you hear about the Lord's brothers, think about the ties of kinship that unite them to Mary, not about her having some new son.

Let us now pay attention to what they say: Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples may also see the works that you do. The works of the Lord were not hidden from his disciples, but they were hidden from them. These brothers or relatives could be related to Christ, but because of their very relationship they felt repugnance to believe in Him. The Gospel says it and it is not our opinion; you just heard it. They continue talking and give him a lesson: No one works in secret if he wants to be known; If you work those wonders, manifest yourself to the world. And immediately the evangelist adds: Not even his brothers believed in Him. Why didn't they believe in Him? Because they were seeking human glory, because in the advice that his brothers seem to give him, they also have the glory of Jesus as their focus. Do you do wonderful things? Well, make yourself known, that is, show yourself to everyone so that everyone will praise you. There was meat to meat; the flesh without God, to the flesh with God. For it is the prudence of the flesh that speaks to the Word, who became flesh and lived with us. 5. What does the Lord answer to all this? Jesus tells them: My time has not yet come, but yours is always soon. What meaning do these words have? Has not the time of Christ come yet? Why has Christ come, if his time has not yet come? Have we not heard the Apostle say: When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son. Therefore, if it was sent in the fullness of time, it was sent when it should, it arrived when it was convenient. What does it mean: My time has not come yet? Understand, brothers, the intention with which those who seemed to advise him as a brother spoke to him. They advised him to seek glory, as if admonishing him with worldly and earthly affection not to remain in darkness and contempt; and what Jesus says: My time has not yet come, is an answer to those who advised him to seek glory: The time of my glory has not yet come. Look how deep there is in this! They invite Him to glory, but He wants humiliation to precede exaltation and humiliation to prepare the way to glory. Those disciples who wanted to sit, one on his right and the other on his left, certainly also sought glory; They looked where, but they didn't see where. The Lord returned them to the road so that they could arrive in order at their homeland.

And, when he taught, he caused admiration among the Jews. Everyone, in my opinion, admired each other, but not everyone converted. And where does the admiration come from? Because many knew the place of his birth and the education he had been given. They had never seen him study; They heard him, however, dispute about the Law, quoting texts of the Law, which no one can do without having read them or read them without having studied; and that's precisely why they couldn't get over their astonishment. But his admiration served as an opportunity to make the truth sink in more deeply. The Lord, in fact, takes advantage of the circumstance of his admiration and words to say something profound, worthy of examination and detailed investigation. Therefore I call attention to your charity, not only so that you may hear fruitfully, but also so that you may pray for me. 3. He says in so few words. It does not say: This doctrine is not my doctrine: but: my doctrine is not mine. If it's not yours, how do you say it's yours? And if it's yours, how do you say it's not? Because you yourself say both things: mine and not mine. Because if I said: This doctrine is not mine, there would be no difficulty. The first thing now, brothers, is to pay attention to the difficulty, and then, in order, wait for the solution. Well, whoever does not see the difficulty involved, how will he understand when the explanation is given? The difficulty is that it says: mine and not mine; There is, apparently, a contradiction. How is it mine and how is it not mine? If we look carefully at what the holy evangelist himself says in the exordium: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God, we will see that the solution to the difficulty depends on this. What then is the doctrine of the Father, if not the Word of the Father? Christ himself is the doctrine of the Father if he is the Word of the Father. It is impossible for the word not to belong to anyone, but it has to be from someone, and he said that He is his doctrine and that it is not his doctrine, because he is the Word of the Father. What is as much yours as yourself? And what is so not yours as you if what you are is someone's? 4. Therefore the Word is also God and is the Word of an immutable doctrine, not expressible by syllables and transitory, but remains with the Father, to which, as a permanent thing, the sounds that go away warn us to turn. The sound that passes does not invite us to the things that happen; invites us to love God. What I have just said is just syllables, which hurt the air until they reach your ears and which pass away with the sound. But what should not happen is what I warned you about, because the one whose love I have exhorted you does not happen; and if you, warned of the passing syllables, turn to Him, you will not pass away either, but will remain with Him who always remains. This, then, is the great thing about the doctrine of Christ, and the sublime and the eternal, which always remains, and to which we are invited by all the things that temporarily pass away when they are true signs and are not uttered maliciously. All the signs that we express with sounds mean something other than sound. God is not two short syllables, nor do we worship or adore two short syllables, nor do we long to reach two short syllables, which almost before they begin stop sounding. Nor is there room in them for the second if the first has not already passed.

Therefore, something great remains, which is God, although the sound does not remain when God is said. Look thus at the doctrine of Christ, and you will arrive at the Word of God; and, when you have reached the Word of God, look carefully that God was the Word, and you will see the truth.

This vice, brothers, that the Lord points out here, is very difficult to avoid in this world: not to judge by appearances, but to always contain oneself within the limits of right judgment. The Lord warned1 the Jews, but he also reminded us; He convinced them of sin, he taught us; He refuted them, he encouraged us. Don't think that this wasn't our thing because we weren't there back then. It was written and it is read, and when it is read we hear it, but as it was said to the Jews. Let us not put ourselves behind our backs, as if to see our enemies rebuked, and let us also do things worthy of being rebuked by Truth itself. The Jews, it is true, judged by appearance; That is why they are not from the New Testament, nor do they have the kingdom of heaven in Christ, nor do they become part of the society of holy angels. They only asked the Lord for material goods: the promised land, and victory over their enemies, and the fertility of their wives, and many children, and abundance of fruits. These goods were promised to him by the Lord, true and good; but he promised them as to carnal men. This and this alone is the Old Testament for them. What is the Old Testament? It is something like an inheritance, which belongs to the old man. We are already renewed, we have become the new man; because the new Man has already arrived. What is so new as being born of a virgin? Well, since there was nothing in Him that needed to be renewed, because He had no sin, a new birth was given to Him. In Him what is new is birth; In us, the new is man. What is the new man? A man whose old age has disappeared through a renewal or new generation. What is the purpose of this renewal?

The judgment is sometimes between father and son; The father complains about his bad son, and the son complains about his father's harshness. In this case, the honor that the son owes him must be preserved for the father: never equal the father and the son in honor; but preference must be given to the son, if he is right; equality between them must be established only on the ground of truth, and in this way due honor is given to the father without equity being neglected. This is how we progress in understanding the words of the Lord; and so that we continue to progress, his grace helps us.

Then those same people who had said: Could it perhaps be true that the princes have recognized that this is the Christ?, raised within themselves the question according to which it should appear to them that this was not the Christ. And then they added: But we know where this one is from; but, when the Christ arrives, no one will know where he is from. What is the origin of this opinion among the Jews, that when the Messiah comes no one will know where he comes from? Because this opinion has its reason. If you carefully examine the Scriptures, you will find, brothers, that the holy Scriptures said of Christ that he would be called a Nazarene. Then it had been predicted in them where he was from. Finally, if the place of his birth is sought, as if it were the same place as the one in which he was born, the Jews were not unaware of this either, because the Scriptures had predicted it. Since, when the Magi, seeing the star, go in search of Him to worship Him, they come to Herod and explain to him what they are looking for and what they want, and he, gathered together those who knew the law, asked them about the place of the birth of the Christ or Messiah, and they answered that Bethlehem of Judah; and they cite a prophetic testimony as well. Then, if the prophets had predicted the place where he was from according to the flesh and the place where his mother gave birth to him, where could the opinion that we have now heard arise among the Jews: When the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from, except from the Scriptures themselves, which left both things said and announced? The Scriptures had predicted where he would be as a man, but like God he was hidden from the wicked, and went to meet the godly. That is why the Jews also said: When the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from. This opinion had its origin in the words of Isaiah: Who will explain his generation? Finally, the Lord himself responds to both things, namely: that they knew where He was from and that they did not know it, as a confirmation of the holy prophecy that had predicted of Him his weakness, according to humanity, and his majesty, according to divinity. 3.

Many miracles were performed after the Lord was resurrected and ascended to heaven. Great wonders were then done by His disciples, but He who had done them for Himself also did them through them, since He Himself had said to them: Without me you can do nothing. When the lame man who was sitting at the door stood up at Peter's voice and began to walk on his own two feet, to the admiration of the people. Peter spoke to them, saying that he had not done this by virtue of any peculiar power of his, but by virtue of him whom they themselves had killed. Many, repenting, exclaimed: What shall we do? Well, they saw themselves as if they were crushed by the weight of an enormous crime of impiety for having killed the one who had the right to their homage and adoration, and they believed that a crime of that kind was something inexpiable. Huge crime, in fact, the sight of which led them to despair; But they should not despair, because for them the Lord had the dignity to pray when He was hanging from the cross. The same goes for the foot; walking he works for the good of all the members; all the other members are silent, and the language speaks to all. We possess, without a doubt, the Holy Spirit if we love the Church. You love it if you remain in its unity and charity. The same Apostle, after speaking of the different gifts that are distributed in different men, as functions of each of the members, adds: I am going to show you a much more excellent way, and begins to speak of charity. He holds it in higher esteem than the gift of the tongues of angels and of man, and more than the miracles of faith and the gift of knowledge and prophecy, and also more than that great work of mercy by which someone gives to the poor everything he possesses, and, finally, also more than the martyrdom of the body. He holds it, in a word, in higher esteem than all these extraordinary things. Possess charity and you will possess everything, because without it everything you may have is of no use to you. And because the Holy Spirit is the author of charity, of which we are speaking (the Holy Spirit is now discussed in the Gospel), listen to the Apostle, who says: The charity of God is spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. 9. Why did the Lord want after his resurrection to give us the Holy Spirit, from whom we have the maximum benefits, since through Him the charity of God was infused into our hearts? What did he want to tell us? In our resurrection, may our charity burn in flames and separate us from the love of the world, so that all of it may run to God. Down here we are born and die; let's not love this; Let us leave here for charity, let us live above for charity, for that charity with which we love God.

Let us see, then, what he promises us: they are not earthly and temporal riches nor honors and power in this world; because we are seeing that all this is also given to men who are bad, so that we do not appreciate them too much. It does not promise us the health of the body either; not that it is not his gift, but because with it he also gives the animals a gift. Not a long life. Is what finally ends long? He does not promise us believers, like something great, longevity or decrepit old age, which everyone wishes for before it arrives and which everyone complains about after it has arrived. Nor does it promise the beauty of the body, which is destroyed by illness or by old age itself, which is so desired. He wants to be beautiful and he wants to be old; These desires are not in harmony with each other; If you are old, you are not beautiful. As soon as old age comes, beauty will flee. The vigor of beauty and the groaning of old age cannot coexist in a man. None of this is promised to us by him who says: He who believes in me, let him come and drink, and from his belly will come rivers of living water. What it promises is eternal life, where there will be nothing to fear, and where we will experience no disturbance, and where we will never leave again, and where we will not die, and where the predecessor is not mourned and the successor is not expected. And because this is what he promises to those of us who love him and are burning with the charity of the Holy Spirit, that is why he did not want to give us that Spirit until we were glorified, so that in his body he would show the life, which we do not have now, but which we hope for in the resurrection.

Well, it is clear that his words have given you great pleasure. Is there anyone among the princes or the Pharisees who has believed in Him? It's just this damned populace, who don't know the law. From there Jesus went to the mountain, but to the Mount of Olives, a fruitful mountain, a mountain of ointment, a mountain of chrism. Where was it appropriate for Christ to teach but on the Mount of Olives? The name of Christ comes from the Greek word Xrisma, which is anointing in Latin. He anointed us precisely because he enabled us to fight the devil. And in the morning he returned again to the temple, and all the people came to him, and sat down and taught him. And no one caught him, because he still did not deign to suffer. 4. Consider now how his enemies tested the meekness of the Lord. The scribes and Pharisees bring him a woman caught in adultery and place her in the middle and say to him: Master, this woman has just been caught in adultery, and Moses commands us in the law to stone this type of women; What do you say? They told him this by tempting him, in order to be able to accuse him. But what could they accuse him of? Had he been caught accidentally in some crime or was that woman considered to be in some way related to Him? What does it mean, then: Tempting him, to have something to accuse him of? Here we see, brothers, how his admirable meekness stands out in the Lord. They realized that He was extremely sweet and meek, since it was already predicted of Him: Gird your sword on your thigh, O most powerful one! Enter with your beauty and loveliness and march with prosperity and reign by your truth, meekness and justice. So he made us know the truth as a teacher, and meekness as a deliverer, and justice as a judge. That is why the prophet predicted that he would reign in the Holy Spirit. When he spoke, the truth was acknowledged, and when he did not rage against his enemies, his meekness was praised. For since his enemies were consumed with hatred and envy for these two things, that is to say, for truth and meekness, they laid a snare for him in the third, that is, in justice. As? The law required stoning adulteresses; and the law, certainly, did not ask to prescribe any injustice: if he said something different from what the law prescribed, he would be surprised at the injustice. So they said among themselves: He is believed to be a friend of the truth and seems kind; His justice must be put to the test with sagacity. Let us present a woman caught in adultery and tell her what the law prescribes about her.

If he orders her to be stoned, he will cease to be kind; and if he judges that she should be acquitted, he will be a transgressor of justice. But they say: In order not to sacrifice his meekness, by which he has made himself so kind to the people,

If his sentence had been that the adulteress not be stoned, it would be evident that it was unjust; and if he had been stoned, he would not appear to be meek. It is justice that sentences: Let the sinner suffer the punishment; but not for sinners; Let the law be executed, but not by its transgressors. This is absolutely not the ruling of justice. And they, wounded by it as by a thick dart, look at themselves and see themselves as prisoners and they all leave there one after another. Only two remain there: misery and mercy. And the Lord, after having plunged the dart of his justice into their hearts, does not even deign to look at how they disappear, but rather turns his sight away from them and once again writes with his finger on the ground. 6. That woman alone and everyone gone, he raised his eyes and fixed them on her. We have already heard the voice of justice; Let us now also hear the voice of meekness. How terrified that woman must have been when she heard the Lord say: Whoever of you is without sin, let him first throw the stone at her! But they look at themselves and, with their flight, confessing themselves guilty, they leave that woman alone with her great sin in the presence of him who had no sin. The promise is made in a future verb; for it does not say "possess," but rather it will possess the light of life. However, he does not say: "Who will follow me", but who follows me. What must be done is expressed in the present tense; On the other hand, what he promises to his faithful fulfillers he says in the future: Whoever follows me will have. Now it follows him and later it will possess him; now he follows him by faith and later he will possess him by vision. While we are united with the body, we are distanced from God: we walk by faith, not by vision. When for vision? When we come into possession of the light of life, when we reach that vision, when this night disappears. For of that day that is to dawn it was said: "In the morning I will be in your presence and I will contemplate you." What does morning mean? When the night of this century passes and the terror of temptations also passes and that lion that wanders around in search of prey is defeated. In the morning he will be next to you and I will see you. But now, brothers, what do we think of as appropriate to this time, if not what is repeated in the psalm: Every night I will wash my bed with my tears and I will water my bed with my tears? I will cry, he says, all night; I will burn, burned by the desire for light. The Lord is seeing my desires, since another psalm says: All my desires are in your presence, and my groans are not hidden from you. Do you want gold? Who sees that desire but God? Whom do you ask, God, as you ask for bread and water, and gold and silver, and wheat? Who do you ask for God but God? God asks God, who promises himself. Let the soul expand its desires, and, having dilated and made the interior of the heart more capable, try to reach the understanding of what neither the eye saw, nor the ear heard, nor ever reached the heart of man. Therefore, brothers, let us follow Christ, the light of the world, so that we do not walk in darkness. The most fearful darkness is the moral darkness, not the darkness of the eyes; And if the darkness of the eyes is fearful, it is not the external darkness, but the internal darkness, which is through which the discernment is made, not between the white and the black, but between the just and the unjust. 2. When Our Lord finished saying these words, the Jews responded: You testify of yourself; your testimony is not true. Before our Lord Jesus Christ came, he had already lit and sent many prophetic lamps before him. One of these torches is John the Baptist, of whom the same light par excellence, which is the Lord Jesus Christ, bore witness as it was not given of any man. The testimony is this: Among those born of women there has been no one greater than John the Baptist. This one, however, who was the greatest among those born of women, says of our Lord Jesus Christ: I certainly baptize you with water; But he who comes is stronger than I, since I am not worthy to untie the straps of his sandals. See how the torch humbles itself before the light of day. The Lord himself testifies that John himself was a lamp. He was, he says, a lamp that burned and shined, and you wanted for a moment to enjoy its light. When the Jews asked the Lord: Tell us with what power you do these things, the Lord, who knew that they considered John the Baptist something great and that the same person whom they held in such high esteem had borne witness to them of the Lord, answered them: I am also going to ask you a question: Tell me: Where is John's baptism from, from heaven or from men? Discomposed, they conversed with each other; Well, if they said that about men, they risked being stoned by the mobs, who considered John a prophet; If they said that it was from heaven, I would give them this answer: He whom you confess to have been given the gift of prophecy from heaven, has testified about me, and from him you have heard by what power I do these things. They realized, therefore, that they would fall into the trap whatever their answer was; and they gave this answer: We don't know. And the Lord's response to them: Nor do I tell you by what power I do these things. I'm not telling you what I know because you don't want to confess what you know.

Having received the truly just rejection, they withdrew full of confusion; and what God the Father says in the psalm through the prophet was fulfilled: I have prepared a torch for my Christ, that is, John himself, and I will cover my enemies with confusion,

The Word was the true light that illuminates every man who comes into this world. If it enlightens every man, then John too; That is why these words from John himself: From his fullness we all receive. Discern these things well so that your mind may make progress in the faith of Christ. Let us not continue to be perpetually children, who eagerly seek milk and reject solid foods. It is time for you to nourish yourself within our mother, the holy Church of Christ, and give up milk and eat more solid foods, but with your mind, not with your belly. Discern, then, this: one is the light that clarifies and another is the light that is clarified. Our eyes are also called lights, and everyone swears by their lights at the same time that they touch their eyes, saying: So long may my lights live. This is an ordinary oath formula. These lights, if they are lights, when your room is closed and without light, let these lights open and illuminate you; this is impossible for them. Just as the eyes that we have on our face, even when they are healthy and open, need external help from light, and, if this is taken away or not given, they do not cease to be healthy and wide open, but, nevertheless, they cannot see, the same thing happens with our mind, which is the eye of the soul: if the light of truth does not radiate in it, if it is not illuminated in a wonderful way by him who clarifies and is not clarified, it is not possible to access neither to wisdom nor to justice. Our path is precisely that: life according to justice. How, then, will he not stumble along the path whom the light does not illuminate? That is why it is a necessity to see in this path, how it is also something great.

Jesus answers and tells them: Although I testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I come from and where I am going. Light makes other things known and also makes itself known. You turn on a light to look for, for example, a tunic, and the light on helps you find the tunic. Do you turn on another light to see what this one looks like? The light that certainly shines is capable of revealing objects hidden in darkness and of showing itself to your eyes. Thus our Lord Jesus Christ established the same difference between his followers and Jewish enemies as between light and darkness: that between those into whom the light of faith penetrated and those whom it only bathed around because they had their eyes closed. As this sun illuminates the face of him who has sight and the face of him who is blind, both, standing and facing the sun, are illuminated in their flesh, but not in their sight, since one sees and the other does not; the sun is in the presence of both, but one is far from that presence; something like this is also the wisdom of God. The • Word of God our Lord Jesus Christ is present everywhere, since truth is everywhere, as is wisdom. He who is in the East understands justice the same as he who is in the West; And is the justice that one understands different from the justice that the other understands? They are distanced by the body, but the gazes of their intelligence are fixed on the same thing. The justice that I am seeing from this place, if it is true justice, is also being seen by the righteous in I don't know what dwellings, separated from me by the flesh, but united with me in the light of the same justice. Then the light bears witness to itself. It appears to healthy eyes and is a testimony of itself to make itself known. And what to judge of the unbelievers? Don't they perhaps have it in their presence? - They have it in their presence, but they don't have the eyes of the heart to see it. Pay attention to the sentence that the Gospel itself pronounces against them: The light shines in the darkness, but the darkness did not know it. Then the Lord speaks and tells the truth: Although I bear witness of myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I come from and where I am going.

you? He is quoted from Isaiah, Daniel, Jeremiah and other holy prophets, and is told how long before Him they came and how far in advance they preceded His coming. This, then, is our answer: the prophets came before Him and predicted His coming. What prophets? one of them asks again. The list of those that are read to us daily is cited. He insists on the question: What are these prophets? Our response: Those who predicted also what we see happening. Reply of the pagan: All these things, he says, are your fictions; You yourselves saw these events and recorded them in writing in whatever books you saw fit, as predictions made long in advance. Here, against our enemies the pagans, we have the testimony of other enemies. We present to them the books of the Jews and tell them: It is true that you and they are enemies of our faith. They are dispersed among the pagans precisely so that we can effectively refute some enemies with the testimony of others. Let the Jews present the book of Isaiah and see if I do not read there: He was led like a sheep to the sacrifice, and like a lamb without bleating before those who sheared him, he did not open his mouth, and because of his humility he was condemned without trial. By his stripes we were healed; We were like sheep out of the way, and He gave Himself for our sins. Here you have a torch. Let's present another...Show the psalm; The prediction of Christ's passion is also read there: They have pierced my hands and my feet and you can count all my bones. And they themselves look at me and contemplate me; They have divided my clothes among themselves and cast lots for my tunic. In you my praise, in the numerous assembly I will confess you. All the ends of the earth will remember and convert to the Lord, and all the nations of the earth will worship him in his presence; for His is the kingdom and He Himself will be the ruler of the nations. One of the enemies blushes that the other provides me with written testimonies. Behold, from the documents provided to me by one enemy, I have obtained victory over the other. 8. See how the lamps also bear witness to the day because of our weakness, since we cannot bear or see the clarity of the day. We ourselves, Christians, are light, it is true, compared to the infidels; That is why the Apostle says: You were darkness for a time, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of light. And in another place: The night is already advanced and the day is approaching; renounce, therefore, the works of darkness and let us put on the weapons of light; As in the clarity of day let us honestly walk. However, since, in comparison with that light to which we eagerly wait to come, it is still night even the very day in which we live, let the apostle Peter be heard, who speaks to us of the voice full of power and magnificence that came upon Christ our Lord: You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. We heard this voice from heaven, he says, when we were with Him on the holy mountain. But, since we were not there nor did we hear the voice coming from heaven, that is why the Apostle tells us: But we have the prophetic oracles, the certainty of which is more firm. You did not hear the voice coming from heaven, but you possess the prophetic oracles, whose certainty is more solid. Our Lord Jesus Christ, therefore foreseeing the existence of impious men, who would unjustly censure His miracles, attributing them to magic, sent the prophets before Him. Because, if he was a magician and through magic he managed to be worshiped after he died, could he, by chance, be a magician before he was born? Give an attentive ear to the prophets, you, O man, who are dead and rotten by the worm of slander; Give an attentive ear to the prophets. I am reading, pay attention to those who preceded the Lord in his coming. We possess, says the apostle Peter, the prophetic words, the certainty of which is more firm, to which it is good that you look carefully as to a torch shining in a dark place until the day comes and the morning star rises in your hearts. 9. When, then, our Lord Jesus Christ comes and, as the apostle Paul also says, brings to light what is hidden in darkness and reveals the thoughts of the heart so that each one may receive from God the praise he deserves, then, in the presence of that day, there will be no need for lamps, nor will the prophets be read to us, nor will the epistles of the Apostle be opened, nor will we go in search of the testimony of John, nor will we even need the Gospel itself.

Let the Gospel say it right now: In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God. You will come to the fountain from which that dew was spread on you. And right there from where the ray of light was thrown reflexively and indirectly on your heart in darkness, you will see the light itself revealed, provided that the purity of your heart can bear it. Dearest ones, what I remember telling you yesterday, John himself tells us: Now we are children of God; but it has not yet been shown what we will be; We know that when He is shown to us, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is. I am realizing that your affections rise with mine to the sky; But this body, subject to corruption, weighs heavily on the soul, and the earthly abode oppresses the intelligence, which thinks a lot.
